case.case_title: Rajaguru, Inspector-General of Police v. Range Bandara and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports (1998) 2 Sri L.R.

clause.text: Additional restrictions apply to armed forces and police for discipline and duty.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether Article 15(8) permits derogation from Article 12 in the case of members of the Police Force otherwise than by means of law (legislation).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner (Inspector-General of Police) argued that Article 15(8) permits derogation from Article 12 in the case of police members without legislation.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents contended that Article 15(8) does not permit derogation from Article 12 except by means of law, meaning legislation only.
key_facts: The petitioner was summarily transferred without following the established transfer procedures.
The petitioner challenged the transfer under Article 126 alleging it was not in accordance with departmental regulations.
The petitioner argued that Article 15(8) allowed the transfer without legislation.
The Court had previously quashed the transfer order.
The petitioner sought review and interpretation of Article 15(8) among other Articles.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court held that Article 15(8) does not permit derogation from Article 12 in the case of police members except by means of law, which means legislation only. The definition of 'law' in the fundamental rights chapter includes only legislation, except in cases of emergency regulations expressly included.
reasoning.application_to_facts: Since the petitioner's transfer was not made by legislation or in accordance with the prescribed legal procedures, the transfer was unlawful under Article 15(8). The Court confirmed that the transfer violated Article 12 rights and could not be justified under Article 15(8) without legislation.
principles_established: Derogation from fundamental rights for police members under Article 15(8) requires legislation.
Summary transfers without following legal procedures violate constitutional protections.
The definition of 'law' in the fundamental rights chapter excludes anything other than legislation except emergency regulations.

outcome.holding: The Court rejected the petitioner's contention that Article 15(8) permits derogation from Article 12 without legislation and upheld the quashing of the transfer order.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 15(8) was central to the Court's reasoning because the petitioner claimed it allowed the transfer without legislation, but the Court interpreted it strictly to require legislation for derogation from fundamental rights of police members, leading to dismissal of the petitioner's claim.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: Article 15 (8) of the Constitution does not permit derogation from Article 12 in the case of members of the Police Force otherwise than by means of law. For the purpose of Article 15 (8) “Law" means only legislation.
